sections.overview: This pipefish is endemic to temperate coastal waters of southern Australia.
sections.identification: Its mottled brown body has pale bars along the back and a raised ridge on the snout.
sections.habitat: It shelters in shallow bays and estuaries among seagrass, algae, reef rubble and shell deposits.
sections.behavior: In Port Phillip Bay, it appears seasonally in large numbers, probably in connection with breeding.
sections.reproduction: The male carries eggs in a brood pouch beneath the tail until the young hatch.
sections.ecology: Its small size and use of seagrass and sheltered reefs place it among the coastal pipefishes of southern Australia.
sections.conservation: Australian sources list it as protected under several state fisheries laws and as marine-listed under the EPBC Act.
